keyTerms.definition: A bell curve in d dimensions.
Mu, where the cloud sits.
Sigma, how the cloud spreads: variances on the diagonal, tilts off-diagonal.

recall.question: What do the mean and covariance describe?
recall.answer: The mean mu is where the cloud sits. The covariance Sigma is how it spreads: diagonal entries are per-axis variances, off-diagonals tilt the cloud.

recall.question: What happens when Sigma is singular?
recall.answer: The density is undefined, |Sigma| = 0. The model needs full-rank data or a regularized Sigma.

keyTerms.definition: Gaussian discriminant analysis: one Gaussian per class, shared covariance.
One covariance shared across classes.
Phi, the fraction of class-1 examples.
p(y = 1 | x) proportional to p(x | y = 1) p(y = 1).

recall.question: Why is the GDA boundary linear?
recall.answer: With shared Sigma the quadratic terms -(1/2) x^T Sigma^{-1} x cancel in the log odds, leaving a linear function of x.

recall.question: What are the GDA MLE formulas?
recall.answer: phi = fraction of class 1, mu_c = class mean, Sigma = pooled scatter / n.

recall.question: When does logistic regression beat GDA?
recall.answer: When the Gaussian shape is wrong: logistic models p(y | x) directly with weaker assumptions.

keyTerms.definition: Learns p(y | x) or a direct map: draws the boundary.
Learns p(x | y) and p(y), then uses Bayes rule: models each side.
The GDA posterior form that does not imply Gaussian features.

recall.question: What is the asymmetry between GDA and logistic regression?
recall.answer: If p(x | y) is Gaussian with shared Sigma, p(y | x) is logistic. The converse is false: logistic p(y | x) does not imply Gaussian p(x | y).

recall.question: On Poisson features, who wins in the large-data limit?
recall.answer: Logistic regression, in the large-data limit. On tiny Gaussian data, GDA wins by needing fewer examples.

sections.title: SL-04: Naive Bayes and conditional independence

keyTerms.definition: Words independent given the class: p(x_j | y) = p(x_j | y, x_k).
The generative spam filter with the independence assumption.
An unseen combination zeroing a whole product.

recall.question: What does the independence assumption buy?
recall.answer: p(x | y) = prod_j p(x_j | y): only 2 * 50,000 parameters instead of 2^50000.

recall.question: What is the zero problem?
recall.answer: An unseen combination zeroes a whole product: p(y=0) prod = 0.4 * 0 * (1/2) = 0, killing class 0 entirely.

recall.question: Why is naive Bayes overconfident on correlated features?
recall.answer: It double-counts the evidence. The probabilities are miscalibrated even when the classifications are right.

keyTerms.definition: phi_j = (1 + count) / (k + n): no probability stays exactly zero.
One fake observation of each outcome added to the counts.

recall.question: What is the Laplace smoothing formula?
recall.answer: Bernoulli word feature: phi_{j|y} = (1 + count) / (2 + n_y). k-sided multinomial: (1 + count_j) / (k + n).

recall.question: What goes wrong with the wrong k?
recall.answer: The denominator is wrong and probabilities do not sum to 1. Match k to the outcome count.

sections.title: SL-06: Bernoulli and multinomial event models

keyTerms.definition: The email is a checklist over the vocabulary; absences count as evidence.
The email is d draws from a word distribution; counts matter, absences do not.

recall.question: How do the two event models treat word absence?
recall.answer: Bernoulli: absences count as evidence. Multinomial: counts matter, absences do not.

recall.question: Why does Bernoulli fail on long documents?
recall.answer: Absence of 49,997 words dominates the product and drowns the signal. Use the multinomial model.

keyTerms.definition: The assumed density shape is wrong, so parameters answer the wrong question.
Predicted probabilities match observed frequencies.
True positives over predicted positives.
True positives over actual positives.

recall.question: What is the difference between misspecification and miscalibration?
recall.answer: Misspecification: the assumed density shape is wrong. Miscalibration: predicted probabilities do not match observed frequencies. A model can classify well and be badly calibrated.

recall.question: Why is accuracy useless at 1 percent positives?
recall.answer: Always-predict-ham gets 0.99 accuracy with 0.0 recall. Precision 0.615 and recall 0.8 distinguish the models; accuracy barely does.
